alignments.note: εἰς governing the articular infinitive takes the English clause-introducer that under rule 61.
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive, unrepresented under rules 23 and 61.
ἰδεῖν → we may see; supplied subject and modal ride with the verb, head on see.
Article of πρόσωπον displaced by the possessive your, which belongs to ὑμῶν under rule 20.
καταρτίσαι → may perfect; the repeated modal is a helper on the second coordinated verb, head on perfect.

Article of ὑστερήματα → the antecedent pronoun that. The ASV recasts the noun this article governs as a finite relative clause, so under rule 92 the article keeps only the word the ASV writes for it and the expressed noun keeps the relativizer, exactly as τοὺς … ἀποστόλους → them that were at GAL.1.17 and οἱ … σπιλάδες → they who are at JUD.1.12 do. Rule 22's that which taken whole is the competing reading and the one this unit previously carried; I did not take it, because rule 31's test makes the article attributive here — ὑστερήματα is an expressed head noun — and rule 22 and the nine corpus units of τό → that which are scoped to a substantival article governing no noun.

ὑστερήματα recast as the predicate of a supplied relative clause → which is lacking. Rule 92 keeps the supplied relativizer and the copula together on the expressed noun, and rule 53 puts the copula on the predicate; head on the lexical word lacking under rule 17.
Article of πίστεως displaced by the possessive your, which belongs to ὑμῶν under rule 20.
πίστεως → in … faith, the case preposition riding with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause.

review_notes: All 18 source and 21 target ids partitioned exactly once; the unit count is unchanged at 18, with 15 aligned and 3 unrepresented as before.

Only s014 and s015 changed: the relativizer which (t016) moves from the article's unit to the noun's, so that the relativizer and the copula stand together on the expressed head noun under rule 92. Heads: t015 that on the article, t018 lacking on the noun.

Reading that which whole on the article under rule 22 remains defensible and is what the verse pass took; it is refused here only because ὑστερήματα is an expressed head noun, which is rule 31's test for telling a substantival article from an attributive one.
No other unit in the chapter is affected: 3:5's ὁ πειράζων already gives the article only its determiner, so the two articles now agree in keeping nothing beyond the word the ASV wrote for them.
